q.e: Malonate resembles succinate and blocks succinic dehydrogenase.

q.q: Match Column I (Condition) with Column II (Effect on enzyme):
q.e: High temp=denatures; Low temp=reversibly inactivates.

q.q: Match Column I (Step) with Column II (Catalytic cycle stage):
q.e: Substrate binding is the first step; product release is the final step of the catalytic cycle.

q.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
(i) Velocity increases indefinitely with increasing substrate concentration
(ii) At Vmax, the enzyme is saturated with substrate
(iii) Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate structurally
q.e: (i) is wrong — velocity plateaus at Vmax, it does not increase indefinitely; (ii) and (iii) are correct.

q.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
(i) The transition state is more stable than the product
(ii) The transition state has higher energy than the substrate
(iii) A catalyst can increase the rate of a reaction by up to about 10 million times in certain cases
q.e: (i) is wrong — the transition state is LESS stable (higher energy) than the product; (ii) and (iii) are correct.

q.q: The duration of the cell cycle in a human cell in culture is about:
q.e: About 24 hours.

q.q: Interphase occupies approximately what percentage of the cell cycle?
q.e: More than 95%.

q.q: The M phase of a cell cycle consists of:
q.e: Nuclear and cytoplasmic division.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Interphase is metabolically inactive (ii) DNA synthesis occurs only in one stage of the cycle (iii) Events of the cell cycle are under genetic control
q.e: (i) is wrong; interphase is metabolically active.

q.q: In the pie diagram of a cell cycle, the smallest sector represents:
q.e: M phase is the shortest (about 1 hour of 24).

q.q: Cytokinesis means division of:
q.e: Cyto = cell.

q.q: In a cell cycle diagram the arrow after M phase leads back to:
q.e: Daughter cells enter G1.

q.q: DNA replication takes place in:
q.e: S = synthesis.

q.q: The quiescent stage of the cell cycle is:
In animal cells, centriole duplication occurs during:
q.e: S phase (in the cytoplasm).

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) S phase doubles the DNA content (ii) S phase doubles the chromosome number (iii) G0 cells are metabolically active
q.e: Chromosome number does not double.

q.q: A cell with 2n = 24 at G1 will have how many chromosomes in G2?
q.e: Chromosome number unchanged.

q.q: In a graph of DNA content vs time, DNA doubles during the phase labelled:
q.e: S phase.

q.q: Example of cells that do not divide in adult animals:
q.e: Heart cells.

q.q: Mitosis was first observed in plant cells by:
q.e: Strasburger (1870).

q.q: Kinetochores are found on:
q.e: On the surface of centromeres.

q.q: The best stage to observe chromosome morphology is:
q.e: Metaphase.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Asters radiate from centrosomes (ii) Nuclear envelope disintegrates completely at the start of metaphase (iii) Golgi complex is clearly visible at the end of prophase
q.e: (iii) is wrong.

q.q: In a diagram of a metaphase cell, the structures connecting chromosomes to the poles are:
q.e: Spindle fibres attach at kinetochores.

q.q: Two asters plus spindle fibres form the:
q.e: Mitotic apparatus.

q.q: A diagram shows chromosomes lined up in one plane at the centre, with each chromatid attached to opposite poles. The stage is:
q.e: Metaphase.

q.q: Centromeres split during:
q.e: Anaphase.

q.q: In anaphase the leading part of a moving chromosome is the:
q.e: Centromere.

q.q: Nuclear envelope reforms during:
q.e: Telophase.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Telophase is the reverse of prophase (ii) Chromosomes lose individuality in telophase (iii) Arms lead the chromosome in anaphase
q.e: (iii) is wrong.

q.q: A diagram shows V-shaped chromosomes moving towards the two poles. The stage is:
q.e: Anaphase.

q.q: Which organelles reappear in telophase?
q.e: Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER.

q.q: A diagram shows two nuclei forming at the poles with a constriction appearing at the centre of an animal cell. The stage is:
q.e: Telophase followed by cytokinesis.

q.q: Cytokinesis in plant cells occurs by:
q.e: Cell plate.

q.q: The cell plate represents the:
q.e: Middle lamella.

q.q: An example of syncytium is:
q.e: Coconut water.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Mitosis restores nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio (ii) Mitosis produces genetic variation (iii) Vegetative reproduction occurs by mitosis
q.e: (ii) is wrong.

q.q: A diagram of a dividing plant cell shows a line forming in the centre and growing towards the walls. It is the:
q.e: Cell plate.

q.q: Continuous growth of plants is due to mitosis in:
q.e: Meristems.

q.q: Multinucleate condition results when:
o: Karyokinesis is not followed by cytokinesis
q.e: Syncytium formation.

q.q: Crossing over occurs during:
q.e: Pachytene.

q.q: The enzyme responsible for crossing over is:
q.e: Recombinase.

q.q: Synaptonemal complex is formed in:
q.e: Zygotene.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) A bivalent has four chromatids (ii) Crossing over occurs between sister chromatids (iii) Chiasmata are seen in diplotene
q.e: (ii) is wrong.

q.q: A diagram shows X-shaped points joining homologous chromosomes. These points are:
q.e: Chiasmata.

q.q: Diplotene may last for months or years in:
q.e: Vertebrate oocytes.

q.q: A diagram of prophase I shows paired homologous chromosomes with a ladder-like structure between them. This structure is the:
q.e: Synaptonemal complex.

q.q: Homologous chromosomes separate during:
q.e: Anaphase I.

q.q: The stage between meiosis I and II is:
q.e: Interkinesis.

q.q: At the end of telophase I, the cells formed are called a:
q.e: Dyad.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Meiosis I is reductional (ii) DNA replicates in interkinesis (iii) Sister chromatids remain joined in anaphase I
q.e: (ii) is wrong.

q.q: A diagram shows paired chromosomes (bivalents) lined up at the centre of a cell. The stage is:
q.e: Bivalents at equator = metaphase I.

q.q: A cell with 2n = 12 after meiosis I has:
q.e: n = 6 with 2 chromatids each.

q.q: A diagram shows chromosomes, each with two chromatids, moving to opposite poles with no centromere splitting. The stage is:
q.e: Anaphase I.

q.q: Centromeres split during meiosis in:
q.e: Anaphase II.

q.q: Meiosis II resembles:
q.e: Mitosis.

q.q: Number of cells formed at the end of meiosis:
q.e: Four haploid cells.

q.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct? (i) Meiosis conserves chromosome number across generations (ii) Meiosis produces genetic variation (iii) Meiosis is responsible for growth
q.e: (iii) is mitosis.

q.q: A diagram shows four haploid cells formed from one cell. This is a:
o: Tetrad of cells after meiosis II
q.e: Tetrad.

q.q: Number of meiotic divisions to form 80 pollen grains:
A diagram shows single chromosomes (with two chromatids) aligned at the equator in two separate haploid cells. The stage is:
q.e: Metaphase II.

q.q: The phase in which the cell actually divides is:
q.e: Actual division happens in M phase.

q.q: Cells that divide only occasionally do so to:
o: Replace cells lost by injury or cell death
q.e: Such cells divide when needed to replace lost cells.

q.q: The proteinaceous components of cytoplasm that help assemble the spindle are:
q.e: Microtubules help in spindle assembly.

q.q: After telophase, cells enter:
o: Cytokinesis and then interphase of the next cycle
q.e: Telophase is followed by cytokinesis and the next interphase.
